Chapter 10: The Role of Humor—Survival, Subversion, and the Power to Heal.
Humor isn’t just about getting a quick laugh or passing the time. It’s so much deeper than that. Really, it’s a survival tool, a clever way to push back against the world when things feel harsh or overwhelming. In some ways, laughter is a kind of superpower. It lets us handle pain, poke holes in authority, and connect with people in ways that words alone just can’t match.
Picture someone going through a rough patch—maybe they’ve just lost their job, ended a relationship, or gotten some scary health news. It’s natural to want to crawl under a rock and just feel sad. But then, someone cracks a joke, or shares a silly story, and suddenly, the weight feels a little lighter. Laughter doesn’t make the pain disappear, but it does make it easier to bear. Even when life feels darkest, humor reminds us there’s still space for a little joy.
And humor can be subversive, too. It’s a powerful way to shine a light on hypocrisy, to deflate egos, and to call out the ridiculous things people in charge sometimes do. Think about that person who has the courage to make everyone laugh at the emperor’s new clothes—they’re quietly shaking things up. With just a joke, they’re speaking truth to power, challenging the system, but doing it with a smile instead of a shout.
But maybe the best thing about humor is its power to heal. Shared laughter creates real connections. It breaks down walls and reminds us we’re not alone in what we’re feeling. When we’re dealing with loss, disappointment, or failure, humor offers a way to move forward. It gives us the chance to start fresh, to see the world from a new angle.
There’s something beautiful about being able to laugh at yourself. It takes humility to admit your own flaws, to celebrate the little imperfections that make you, you. When you can find the humor in your own mistakes, you’re letting go of the need to have everything under control. And honestly, the folks who can laugh at themselves? They’re usually the ones who find the most peace in life.
